author: kshemaraja
summary: Twenty sutras with the author's own commentary, presenting the Pratyabhijna ("recognition") philosophy for those new to it.
whyRead: It is the classic introduction to the recognition school. In twenty sutras it explains how the world is the free self-expression of consciousness and how the individual recognises itself as Shiva.
questions: If everything is consciousness, why do I feel limited?
What does it mean to recognise oneself?

keyTeachings.title: Consciousness as free cause of the world
keyTeachings.text: The first sutra presents consciousness (chiti), acting in freedom (svatantrya), as the cause of the whole world. The world is its self-manifestation, not an illusion to be rejected.

keyTeachings.title: Contraction and the individual
keyTeachings.text: The individual is consciousness in a contracted form. The same consciousness appears as limited subject and object through its own power.

keyTeachings.title: The five acts
keyTeachings.text: Shiva performs five acts: emission, maintenance, withdrawal, concealment and grace. The text suggests that the individual performs these too, in every act of experience.

keyTeachings.title: Recognition as liberation
keyTeachings.text: Liberation is recognising (pratyabhijna) that one is already Shiva, a shift in self-understanding rather than the acquisition of something new.

passages.about: Free consciousness as the cause of the world
